rv.q: In her hands, Cyrano becomes a giddy and sensitive celebration of love; a feel-good romp full of deep pleasures that seem to reach beyond the space in which we experience them.

In setting this within a theatre, with minor players literally sidelined, and a departure from the storyline to seek an alternative, happier, ending, this Cyrano is both heartwarming and a challenge to heteronormacy.
The company is determined to have an upbeat ending and there’s fun to be had along the way involving party hats and streamers.

cn.t: Critics largely embrace this gender-flipped, queer retelling of Rostand's classic, praising Virginia Gay's sharp writing and performance. A witty, romantic reimagining that's "rough around the edges" but mostly wins over audiences.
